# Floor and Ceiling — Translate Integer Constraints

## The identity to remember

$$
\left\lceil\frac ab\right\rceil=\left\lfloor\frac{a+b-1}{b}\right\rfloor
$$

**Every symbol explained:** a is a nonnegative integer number of items; b is positive integer capacity per batch; ceil rounds up, floor rounds down. The right identity applies to integers a≥0,b>0.

**Substitute actual numbers:** With 17 items in batches of 5, ceil(17/5)=ceil(3.4)=4. Formula floor((17+5−1)/5)=floor(21/5)=4.

## Why it is true

Write a=qb+r with 0≤r<b. If r=0, both expressions equal q. If r>0, both equal q+1. Therefore the integer expression computes the number of batches.

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

Use for number of pages, servers, trips, rounds or blocks when partial final groups need a whole slot.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

For nonnegative fixed-width integers, a+b−1 can overflow; alternative safe code uses a/b+(a%b!=0). Negative a requires a different rounding proof.

## Your turn

Compute how many 64-byte blocks store 1000 bytes.

**Memory rule:** Translate the inequality into a statement about maximum, minimum or impossible values, then prove it.
